svg.title: No profile photo
svg.desc:
Placeholder avatar for the circular frames in the My Account pages: .czap-avatar in the hero and .czap-photo__preview in the profile form.
It replaces user.png there. That file is a 128px line drawing whose ink runs edge to edge (the head touches row 0, the torso outline sits on row 127), so inside a circular frame it could only be letterboxed until its 3px strokes fell under a pixel, or clipped through the shoulders. user.png is untouched and still used by the header avatars, which are not circular.
This one is drawn for a circle. Three things make it fit: solid shapes instead of hairlines, so nothing breaks up at 76px; a warm palette taken from the account hero, so it belongs to the card it sits on rather than dropping a grey blob into a peach gradient; and shoulders that deliberately reach the bottom edge, with their widest point (y is about 52) well inside the circle, so the frame crops only the part of the bust that is meant to run off it.
account-suite.css renders it with object-fit cover and no padding, which turns the background square below into the disc.
Note for editors: this is XML, so a comment can never contain two hyphens in a row. A CSS custom property written out in full inside a comment makes the whole file unparseable and the browser silently draws a broken image. That is why this text lives in a desc element instead. Note also that .htaccess marks every asset immutable for a year, so the views load this through add_ver() and an edit here only reaches a browser because of that.
